points.quote: For assessed coursework, you must disclose any use of GenAI.
points.anchor: Using GenAI tools in your studies and assessments
points.gist: For assessed coursework, any use of GenAI must be disclosed.

points.quote: GenAI can be a valuable learning aid for non-assessed tasks.
points.anchor: Using GenAI tools in your studies and assessments
points.gist: GenAI can be a valuable learning aid for non-assessed tasks.

points.quote: However, you must always verify a GenAI’s output using your critical thinking skills to address ethical considerations and check accuracy.
points.anchor: Using GenAI tools in your studies and assessments
points.gist: You must always verify GenAI output using critical thinking, to address ethical considerations and check accuracy.

points.quote: You can access guides and courses on the GenAI for students Padlet board, including prompting, Grammarly AI, GenAI research tools, and FAQs.
points.gist: A GenAI for students Padlet board has guides and courses on prompting, Grammarly AI, GenAI research tools and FAQs.

points.quote: To access these, sign in to Blackboard and access the Blackboard site ‘Generative AI at Westminster’ from your ‘My Modules and Courses’ page.
points.gist: Short GenAI courses are on the Blackboard site 'Generative AI at Westminster', reached from the My Modules and Courses page.

points.quote: We have also produced guidance on the use of Generative AI for Doctoral Researchers, which should be read in conjunction with the above.
points.anchor: Using GenAI tools in your studies and assessments
points.gist: Separate guidance for Doctoral Researchers exists and should be read together with the student guidance.
